naslov: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ Hastens to Bring People into Jannah

segmenti.tekst: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdulillah, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Rasulillah, wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi, amma ba'd.

Respected attendees, as you had the opportunity to read in the announcement of this evening's halaqah (study circle) of ours, it bears the title: Our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), hastened and ran in order to guide people to the right path.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is the most well-meaning of people, the most sincere, the most compassionate towards his ummah. And that is why Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "An-nabiyyu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim wa azwajuhu ummahatuhum."

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is closer to the believers than they are to themselves. So, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, has a greater claim on us than our parents, than our family, than our children, than our wealth, and than our very selves. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, has a greater claim on each one of us.

And we are obliged to love the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, more than we love ourselves, as has come in the hadith in Bukhari and Muslim from Umar, radiyallahu anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), that Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than all people, than all creatures, except myself."

And then the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said to him: "You will not be, O Umar, a true believer until you love me more than you love yourself." Why does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, have a greater claim on us than we ourselves? Because the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam,

wishes good for us more than we wish good for ourselves. And regarding this verse, Ibn al-Qayyim, rahimahullah, mentions a variant reading (qira'ah) that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is the spiritual father of the believers. Because biologically our parents are the means by which we came into this world and live this physical, material way of life,

while the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is the cause of our spiritual birth and of our eternal happiness and eternal success both in the dunya (this world) and in the akhirah (Hereafter). And that is why, on the Day of Judgement, everyone will be concerned about himself, even the prophets of Allah, from Nuh, from Adam, through Nuh, through Ibrahim, Musa and Isa – each of them will say: "Nafsi, nafsi, nafsi" – my soul, my soul, or woe is me, so that I may save myself. But the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, will say: "Ummati, ya Rabbi, ummati, ya Rabbi, ummati, ya Rabbi" –

my ummah, O Lord, my ummah, O Lord, my ummah, O Lord. On one occasion Aisha, radiyallahu anha, says, she saw that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was in a good mood, so she said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for me." And Aisha said… then the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "O dear Allah, forgive Aisha all her sins, both what she has done and what she will do, small and great, and all sins, and forgive."

And Aisha relaxed and cheered up and began to laugh from contentment and happiness, and then the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "O Aisha, every day, in every prayer, I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, with this supplication for my ummah."

The Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, wished so much good for mankind and wished so much good for everyone, for his relatives and for all people, that Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, admonished him and said to him: "Will you destroy yourself because they will not believe?"

Meaning, will you allow yourself to waste away both physically and psychologically, to have your heart crushed to pieces, because people will not believe? Yours is only, your obligation is only to convey, and Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the One who guides people to the right path. There was no opportunity that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, missed and did not use to guide people to the right path.

He used the Hajj: when all the tribes came to perform the Hajj, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, went from tribe to tribe, from tent to tent, saying: "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah. Qulu la ilaha illallah tuflihu" – say "La ilaha illallah", enter Islam, save yourselves.

Although he experienced unpleasantness, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, wanted, both out of his compassion and out of his goodness, to guide all of mankind to the right path. One of the situations that is the topic and the core of our lecture tonight is the moment when his paternal uncle Abu Talib was on his deathbed.

When he was dying and fell ill with the illness from which he would pass away, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, immediately ran and went in to him, finding that Abu Jahl and Umayyah ibn [unclear] were already in his presence.

And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said to Abu Talib: "Say just this one single sentence, and I will testify before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, that you uttered it, that you affirmed it and that you lived by it. Say this sentence; it will be your pledge for entering, in sha Allahu ta'ala, in sha Allahu ta'ala, into Jannah (Paradise)."

And then Abu Jahl and Umayyah ibn Khalaf turned to Abu Talib, saying to him: "Atarghabu 'an millati 'Abdil-Muttalib?" – "Are you rejecting the religion of your father Abd al-Muttalib?" And the Prophet was saying to him: "Say La ilaha illallah, say La ilaha illallah."

They were saying to him: "Will you renounce the religion of your forefathers? Will you renounce the religion of your forefathers?" They pressed him. And, it is said, they continually insisted and pressed and tried to persuade him.

And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, also kept advising him constantly, until his last words, which were – until he uttered his last words before death – "Huwa 'ala millati 'Abdil-Muttalib." So, he is on the religion of his ancestors, of Abd al-Muttalib, and he passed away. And he passed away upon falsehood and passed away upon unbelief, that is, shirk.

And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, saddened by that moment and by the loss that befell his uncle, said: "I will ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for you, to forgive your sins, until Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, forbids me."

And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, revealed the verses: "It is not fitting for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, for the polytheist unbelievers, after it has become clear to them that they are the inhabitants of Jahannam (Hellfire), even if they are their relatives."

And Allah the Exalted revealed: "Truly, you cannot guide to the right path whomever you wish." This is an incredible story. Abu Talib is the paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. He is the brother of Abdullah, the father of the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, through both father and mother.

And Abu Talib made a great contribution to the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and a great contribution to the religion of Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, so that it would spread, so that it would become established and firm in Makkah. Abu Talib was a shield for the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Do you know what he used to say? "Wallahi lan yasilu ilayka bi jam'ihim hatta uwassada fit-turabi dafina." All of Makkah was against the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. He says: "By Allah, they will not come, will not reach you, except over my dead body."

First they would have to kill me and cut off my head, and only then reach you. And he used to say: "وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ بِأَنَّ دِينَ مُحَمَّدٍ مِنْ خَيْرِ أَدْيَانِ الْبَرِيَّةِ دِينَا" [unclear] "لَوْلَا الْمَلَامَةُ أَوْ حَذَارُ مَسَبَّةٍ لَوَجَدْتَنِي سَمْحًا بِذَاكَ مُبِينَا" – and were it not for the shame, and were it not for the fear that my people would reproach me, I too would follow you, O Muhammad. Look what words these are! He says: the best religion is the religion of Muhammad, and the path of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is the right path. But were it not for the shame,
and were it not for the fear that the Quraysh would say of me: "He has abandoned the religion of his forefathers and was afraid of death," he says, "I would be the first to follow you."

Abu Talib protected him from early childhood. He protected him even when everyone boycotted him. Abu Talib did not allow anyone to trouble or insult the Prophet Muhammad, Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

And that is what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, points to in the Qur'an: they protect the Prophet – Abu Talib and certain of his relatives – but they keep away from the Prophet. They protect him because he belongs to their family, but they are far from his religion, from his ideology, and from the faith and the truth to which he, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, calls.

Here, from this hadith, from this event, we can learn a great number, a great number of lessons. First of all, the effort of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to guide people. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, after Allah the Exalted said to him: "وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ" – and warn your nearest kin, your closest relatives, and your sincere helpers among them –

the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, immediately gathered them on the hill of Safa and said to them: "Would you believe me if I informed you that behind this hill there is an enemy who wants to attack you?" They say: "Of course we would believe you.

[unclear] We have never known you to lie to us. You have never lied to us. 100% – whatever you tell us, it is the truth." And then the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says to them: "I am a clear warner to you from Allah, that this religion you are upon is falsehood and batil,

that the shirk you ascribe to Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, is a path that will lead you to Jahannam." Abu Lahab stood up – it was said by his other uncle, whose name was Abd al-Uzza. Abu Talib's name was Abd Manaf, and his uncle Abu Lahab's name was Abd al-Uzza, servant of the false deity al-Uzza – he said: "Tabban laka, a li hadha jama'tana?" – "May you perish! Is it only for this, for this that you gathered us?" But what is the point?

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, took part there. This should be our motto and our motivation with regard to our relatives, and with regard to our people, and with regard to all of mankind: that we be well-meaning towards people, that we wish them khayr and wish them good, and that we treat them in the most beautiful way and address them in the most beautiful way.

So, those people who have not understood the truth – it is obligatory to address them with the most beautiful words and to use the gentlest and most beautiful methods in calling, as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala… And by no means should a person approach them full of hatred, full of aversion, with ugly, repulsive traits, and address them in that way while wishing them the right path and calling them, so, [unclear].

There is no benefit in that, no effect. You must wish for the person who is in the greatest error what you wish for yourself, for yourself: that you wish him guidance, that you wish him, that you wish him khayr. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in Madinah – a boy from the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), from the Children of Israel, fell ill.

A boy of about ten years, as Imam Bukhari records. As soon as the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, heard, he went to him and said to him: "O young lad, say La ilaha illallah, say La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah." And this boy looked at his father, seeking with his gaze permission from his father as to what to do, even though he knew that Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was upon the truth and upon the right path.

And his father said to him: "There is Abul-Qasim, obey Abul-Qasim, listen to him." And that boy said: "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah," and gave up his soul. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, happy, joyful, elated, came out of that house and said: "Allah has saved him from the fire of Jahannam through my word and by my means." And that is why, my dear brothers, a great number of our people live in heedlessness and negligence (ghaflah), even though our people are basically a good people.

Our people went through communism, ignorance of God, atheism, an incredibly terrible and great jahiliyyah, ignorance of God and ignorance. And that is why that period and that ideology left devastation among our people and among our folk.

And that is why you will find a great number of our compatriots who say "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah" but have nothing else of worship and good deeds in their lives: neither prayer, nor fasting, nor zakat, nor Hajj, nor any other good deed, and especially prayer.

That, then, is a deviation. And a Muslim who has understood the guidance, who has understood the right path, who has set out on the right path, who has listened to his scholars, his hodjas, his teachers (muderris), at the hutbas (Friday sermons), at the lessons, while his parents do not pray – he must not sleep. In other words: how worried he should be, how much he should pray to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, how hard he should strive to guide them to the right path.

He cannot be at peace. Your relatives are not on the right path, and you are so calm, cold-blooded, and not interested in what state they are in? I know a student who studied the Sharia sciences in Arab countries, in the Arab world.

When he came home for the summer holidays, he would go into the neighbourhood (mahala) and from house to house visit all his relatives and all his neighbours, invite them to the prayer, invite them to obey Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, because he feared he would not find them alive the following year.

He wanted to convey the proof to them, that is, to establish the proof for them and to convey the truth to them. And my dear brothers and respected attendees, whoever invests effort in the way of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, Allah will give him a good, well, result.

By God, the Messenger of Allah was tireless on the path of truth and on the path of good. Here we see that Abu Talib passed away as a non-Muslim. There are some factions that have tried to fabricate some hadiths, to bring Abu Talib into Jannah, by way of example without evidence, out of pity for the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam:

he is the Prophet's, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, uncle, and so on, and so on. However, that is an incorrect [unclear]. We are sorry that Abu Talib did not pronounce the shahadah, that he did not become a Muslim. However, remember one thing and one great fact: Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, is not unjust towards His servants.

Allah is not unjust towards His servants. And had Abu Talib shown enough interest, Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, … And that truth which we repeat in our hutbas and speeches: "Whomever Allah guides to the right path, he is rightly guided, and whomever Allah leaves in error, for him there is no guidance" – of course, at first glance this fact may perhaps seem, God forbid, unjust. What does it mean: whomever Allah guides to the right path, he is guided; whomever Allah leaves in error, he will find no guidance? Whom does Allah guide to the right path? Allah guides to the right path

the one who wants guidance and strives to attain it; the one who shows interest and signs that he wants guidance – Allah will surely guide him. And whom does Allah leave in error? The one who wants error, and the one who rejects warnings, and the one whom the warners have warned so many times and delivered proof to, but he rejected it all – he has deliberately chosen error, and so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, left him, left him, then, in error.

So every argument was knocked out of Abu Talib's hands. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, spoke to him, but he gave preference to certain customs and certain practices and certain incorrect phenomena and rules that prevailed in that society over the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and over the truth that had become clear to him.

And that is why it is not enough for a person merely to know and recognise the truth; he must submit to it. Our people, for example, a great number of people say: "I believe in Allah, there is some force," and so on, "our religion is the best religion." However, there is nothing of the religion in their deeds and in their practice.

If he passes away in such states and in such a condition, it will not benefit him with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Why? Because Iblis, la'natullahi alayh (Allah's curse be upon him), knows Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala. He believes that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the truth, and he swears by Allah.

Iblis swears by Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. But he is the greatest enemy and he will be at the bottom of the fire of Jahannam. Why? Because he did not submit. So if a person only claims: "I am convinced that Islam is the truth, I believe in Allah, I believe in the prophets," but does none of the good deeds that confirm, confirm that belief of his, it will not benefit him with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Do you see? Abu Talib used to say: "The best religion is the religion of Muhammad," but he did not submit.

He did not submit. Next, when someone passes away as a non-Muslim, it is not permissible for us to direct supplication (dua) to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for him. If it is known that someone passed away committing acts of unbelief, that he blasphemed Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentioned Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in the ugliest way, denied the religion of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and the like, it is not permissible for you to make dua for him, to pray to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for him.

At certain moments ignorance among some Muslims reaches such a level that, simply, for those who are declared non-Muslims, even the leaders of great errors, when they pass away, our ignorance and [unclear]… It cannot be said like that; it is not fitting.
It is not right. You know, recently, when one of their great leaders passed away, our people said: "May Allah have mercy on him, may He bless him, he helped, he did, he did…" You can't, man!

"May Allah forgive him" – you can't. If he was [unclear]. You can't. You may not pray to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, pray for him. Next, in this case and in this event, one great message is the importance of a good environment and good company.
The importance of what company a person keeps, and what environment he finds himself in, and what environment he spends his time in. Look what bad friends mean. Look what bad company means.

Abu Jahl and Umayyah ibn Khalaf led Abu Talib into the fire of Jahannam. They played the role of Shaytan, and they did not leave him until he gave up his soul. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, implored him, begged him, tried to persuade him, while they, like devils, said: "Will you abandon the religion of your father, will you abandon the religion of your father?" In that last moment they did not leave him to reflect a little, to make a decision, that is, in some free atmosphere; rather, they simply pressed him so hard that he said: he is on the religion of his forefathers.

And that is why, my dear brothers, respected believers, it is very important that you have a good friend as a companion, a sincere person as a companion. Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful." The Arabs say of a friend: "as-sahib sahib" – the sahib, or friend, is the one who pulls you: either he pulls you towards good (khayr), or he pulls you towards evil,

depending on what his orientation is. And that is why, dear parents, dear friends, direct your children and your youth to keep company with quality people, with those who perform the prayer, with those who believe in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, with those from good families and good households.

That is one of the great reasons for a person to remain steadfast on the right path. Also, that Muslims live in a Muslim environment. It is an obligation for Muslims to live in a Muslim environment. Because the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, disowns a Muslim who lives in a non-Muslim environment.

Why? Because the one who lives in such a negative atmosphere and bad surroundings will, over time, become part of that atmosphere. He will melt away, disappear, assimilate, just as a sugar cube dissolves in a glass of water.
That is how identity melts away, that is how faith disappears, that is how virtues disappear. And a person by nature takes on the influence of those with whom he keeps company.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, used to say that herdsmen, people who tend cows and sheep and camels, take on the traits of the animals they keep company with. So shepherds of sheep are gentle, quiet, calm, humble.

And those who tend horses, who tend camels – the camel is an arrogant animal – they are arrogant, proud. [unclear] a professor, about those Bedouins who tend camels, who spend time only with camels, he says: you may sit with him and beside him for three days, three nights, and he will not say a single word to you.

Arrogant, like a camel. He takes on the traits of the camel. Well, imagine how a person influences a person – a person who speaks, who talks, who influences, who insists, who presses, who offers. That is why it is very important, very significant that we create a healthy environment.

This is a healthy environment. But this healthy environment and this health we must carry over to our schools, our neighbourhoods, to our homes and into our institutions and into all our towns and villages and neighbourhoods. Wherever our people live, there must be a healthy environment.

Because, as one of the great Islamic scholars says – may Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, ease his condition [unclear] – today the conflict between the Muslims and this atheistic, jahili civilisation that dominates is not a conflict between Islam and falsehood, between truth and falsehood, but a conflict between humanity and inhumanity.

Humanity or inhumanity. Have you not seen these days what documents have come out? Three and a half million, or three million different documents of that over there [unclear], and of that so-called elite that did the most abominable things, and yet rules the world, does the most abominable things.

And they talk to us about [unclear] of children, people, women, animals, and the like. They are going to talk to us, the Muslims, about that? Their fitrah (innate nature) is perverted; humanity has completely disappeared from their souls and their lives. Well, when we see that, my dear brothers and respected sisters, we must hold on to our religion even more, even more firmly, with our molar teeth, as the Prophet Muhammad said. We have nothing to be ashamed of in our religion. We have no reason to be ashamed of anything in our religion. Everything that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has prescribed – hold firmly to that ruling.

There lies for you and for your family, you and your household, pride, dignity and victory, in sha Allah, in sha Allahu ta'ala. Next, guidance is in the hands of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Guidance is in the hands of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

However much you strive, Allah is the One who opens, who opens, then, the hearts, and He is the One who guides people to the right path. It is interesting that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, had four paternal uncles. Two of his uncles, who had beautiful names, namely Hamzah and Abbas, accepted Islam.
And two of his uncles, who had ugly names, namely Abd Manaf, Abu Talib, and Abd al-Uzza, Abu Lahab, remained in unbelief.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, loved beautiful names. And he loved to interpret them and draw positive messages and optimism from those names. For example, the tribe of Aslam came by, and he said: "Aslam, salamaha Allah."

"Aslam" – from the word for "peace" and "safety" – he said: the tribe of Aslam – "salamaha Allah" – may Allah keep them safe. He saw the tribe of Ghifar, from the word "ghafara", meaning to forgive, and he said: "Ghifaru ghafarallahu laha" – the tribe of Ghifar, may Allah forgive their sins.

A man named Suhayl came at Hudaybiyyah – the name Suhayl means ease, simplicity – and he came in as a negotiator from the other side. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Here is this Suhayl. Suhayl is coming – sahula amrukum."

You will easily conclude the matter with him. And when the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, came across some ugly name, he would order the name to be changed. In particular, such as Abd ash-Shams – servant of the sun, Abd al-Uzza – servant of, I don't know, some false deity, etc., al-Hakam – the judge – he would change the name.

Abu Jahl was Abul-Hakam, and the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, gave him the nickname Abu Jahl. Abul-Hakam means father of the judge and so on, and then the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, told him: "No, you are the father of the greatest ignorance."

And so he became known, and until the Day of Judgement he is best known by that. That is why, my dear brothers, it is an obligation for a person to speak good words and always to have a positive outlook. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: "Kana yu'jibuhul-fa'lu wal-kalimatut-tayyibah" –

[unclear] he liked optimism and a good word. Beautiful names, beautiful titles. And children are given beautiful names. We used to give beautiful names, we Muslims here in Sandžak, in Bosnia and so on. See what beautiful names we used to give, Muslim names, purely Muslim names,

Arabic names, to our children. And then communism came. Communism crushed us, brothers. And you don't know… I wouldn't want to mention now some names that mean nothing, brothers, mean nothing, in any language: neither in Bosnian, nor in Albanian, nor in Turkish, nor in Arabic – in no language do they have any meaning.

And our people say: "An international name." What is an international name? That, O my Lord, that is a non-Muslim name; they just came up with excuses for themselves that way. And I also know another great error that, for example, they practised and carried out, which is, you know: a child is born and they take him to the hodja and say: "Hodja, you give him a name, a Muslim one: Muhammad, Ahmad, Hasan, [unclear]," while he will actually be called, I don't know, something… let no one take offence, I don't want to mention these names.

After some actor, for example… Muslims give names – terrible, terrible! He says: "What is his name?" He says: "Legally his name is this, and here for the dunya it's that." What does that mean? You are creating a split personality, you are making him into one. Traces of secularism.

So, on the Day of Judgement, when it comes, let him be called by this name, and for the dunya let him have some worldly name over here. [unclear] That is the error. What a deviation that is! And it all comes from ignorance, from the desire to ingratiate ourselves and to follow those who have something of less value compared to our culture, our identity, to what we have.

And look how Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, guided Hamzah and Abbas to the right path, while, unfortunately, these two, who perhaps took pride in those names, in being servants of something other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – they ended up as servants of those false creations.

Imam Bukhari included this hadith in his book, in the "Sahih", and he said: "Chapter on when a polytheist on his deathbed says La ilaha illallah." Then you ask yourself: how so, when a polytheist on his deathbed says La ilaha illallah? This polytheist did not say La ilaha illallah. But with this heading of his, Bukhari sends us the message that whoever says La ilaha illallah will enter Jannah, and that the only ticket by which one can enter Jannah is the words "La ilaha illallah", as the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, used to say: "La yadkhulul-jannata illa nafsun mu'minah" –

only a believing soul will enter Jannah, only a soul that said "La ilaha illallah". That is why, my dear brothers, respected sisters, we who utter "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah", we who belong to this shahadah and to this truth, we are the happiest of people, we are the most privileged, we are the most chosen, we are the most honoured by Allah. So rejoice – "wa bashshiril-mu'minin" – rejoice, give glad tidings to the believers – and preserve what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has

granted you: preserve it and spread it. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to have mercy on us, to make us among those who call to the shahadah, and to make us among those whose last words will be "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur-Rasulullah", that the angels of mercy will receive us, and that He will, in sha Allahu ta'ala, gladden us with the most beautiful rewards on the Day of Judgement, in the company of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam,
